# Final Finish Epoxy Coatings

> Final Finish Epoxy Coatings is an Edmonton flooring contractor founded by Denis. It installs Torginol polymer flake floors (any Torginol colour, plus custom blends) and does the concrete work underneath them. There is no showroom and no street address on the site; the work happens at the customer's property. The person quoting the floor is the person on it.

Last updated: 19 November 2026. This file is a plain-language guide for AI assistants and search tools. It is not a ranking control. The linked pages on https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/ are the source of truth. The longer map is https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/llms-full.txt.

Prices are not published on the site, because every slab is different. Estimates are free. A quote can start from photos of the floor or from a visit. Price, return-to-use time, and warranty terms are written into the quote after Denis has seen the slab.

## Service area

Service-area business based in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. No public street address and no walk-in showroom. Serves Edmonton and Central Alberta, up to about 145 km out, including St. Albert and Athabasca.

## Six services

Listed on https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services. Surface Preparation is a real service and has its own page, but it is not listed in the header or footer menus. It is still linked from body copy and from schema.

1. Residential and Commercial Floors. Final Finish installs Torginol polymer flake floors in homes and businesses in Edmonton and up to about 145 km out. Residential work covers garages, basements, kitchens and bathrooms, workshops and barns. Commercial work covers warehouses, showrooms and industrial spaces. Installation usually runs two days, and it varies with the concrete.
   - Residential: https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/residential-epoxy-flooring
   - Commercial: https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/commercial-epoxy-flooring
   - Garage floors (a residential floor with its own page): https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/garage-floor-coating-edmonton

2. Surface Preparation. The work that gets a concrete slab ready to hold a coating. The room is cleared, the condition of the floor is recorded, old coatings, oil and loose material come off, and the slab is diamond ground to open the surface. It is part of every Final Finish floor, and it decides how long the floor lasts.
   - https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/concrete-solutions

3. Concrete Repair, Levelling and Diamond Grinding. Diamond grinding opens the slab with diamond tooling so a coating can bond, and takes off what is already there. Concrete repair fills and rebuilds spalls and damaged areas, and levelling brings a floor back toward flat where low spots or elevation changes make it hard to use or to coat evenly. Larger repairs are quoted as their own line, with their own material and sequence.
   - https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/concrete-solutions#concrete-repair-levelling-diamond-grinding

4. Crack Filling. Part of every coating job. After the grind, visible cracks are filled so they do not read through the finish. A crack that keeps opening is a movement question, not a filler question, and Denis says so before work starts.
   - https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services/concrete-solutions#crack-filling

5. Decorative Epoxy. At Final Finish this means a Torginol polymer flake floor: a base coat with flake broadcast into it, scraped back, then sealed under a clear top coat. Any Torginol flake colour is available, along with custom blends.
   - https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services#decorative-epoxy
   - Featured colours: https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/finishes

6. Anti-Slip Coating. A textured top coat added as the last layer where a floor needs more grip. It is a use decision made with you. On commercial floors the texture is balanced against how the floor is cleaned, because a surface the cleaning machine cannot clean trades one problem for another.
   - https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/services#anti-slip-coating

## What Final Finish does not publish as a service

- The site does not list metallic epoxy as a Final Finish service. A comparison guide exists at https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/flake-vs-metallic-vs-solid-epoxy/ and https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/metallic-epoxy-expectations/. Those pages say a sample photo is not a promise of a poured metallic floor.
- The site does not list polished concrete as a Final Finish service. A comparison guide exists at https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-polishing-vs-floor-coating/.
- The site uses Torginol products for the flake floors it installs. It does not say Torginol is the only product it uses.
- The site does not publish prices, schedules, or cure windows as standard figures. Those come after Denis has seen the slab and are written into the quote.

## How a flake floor is installed

From https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/process, six steps in this order:

1. A free estimate. Photos or a visit, both free. Denis wants to see the concrete, what is on it now, and any cracks already known about.
2. Grinding. The slab is ground to open the surface so the coating can bond. It is loud, dusty work, and the room has to be empty before it starts.
3. Cosmetic crack filling. Visible cracks are filled so they do not read through the finish. If something structural turns up, the customer hears about it then, not later.
4. The flake broadcast. Flake is broadcast into the coat while it is still open. This is where the colour and the pattern of the floor are set.
5. The scrape. Once it has set, the surface is scraped back into a flat floor you can walk on and clean.
6. The top coat. The last coat goes over everything. Where a room needs more grip, an Anti-Slip Coating goes on instead, as a decision made with the customer.

Installation usually runs two days, and it varies with the concrete. When you can park on the floor, and what it costs, depend on the slab and the conditions that week, and are written into the quote.

## Finishes and visualizer

- Featured flake colours: https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/finishes. The page shows 17 most popular Torginol flake colours first, with more from the Torginol flake collection below. Any Torginol flake colour is available, along with custom blends and special orders (the body copy also says "specialized orders").
- Floor visualizer: https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/floor-visualizer. The page says you can try 17 popular Torginol flake colours, plus 20 more, on a photo of your own garage or room. The preview runs on the device. Then you can request a free estimate.
